what_this_measures: payload_chars is len() of the full tools/list response of the in-process server,
serialised as compact sorted JSON: every tool's name, description, input schema,
output schema and meta. It is what a client pays, in every conversation, before
the agent has done anything. About 3.5 chars per token, so 22,592 chars is
roughly 6,500 tokens.
The 5 component counts sum to payload_chars and say where the bytes are, so a
regression can be attributed instead of merely detected. Moving prose out of a
docstring and into a parameter description moves bytes between the first 2
components and saves nothing.
structural_chars is the floor: JSON braces, parameter names, types, defaults and
anyOf null wrappers. It only moves when a tool or a parameter is added or removed.
output_schema_chars is 26 copies of a schema declaring that the tool returns a
string, 1 per tool except screenshot, which returns an image. Passing
output_schema=None to the tool decorator would delete all 2,860 of them, and
would also stop every tool returning structuredContent, so a client reading
result.data would get nothing. That is a protocol change rather than a prose
change, so it was left alone on purpose rather than overlooked.
The 2026-08-06 re-measure raised payload_chars from 22,263 by 329: 231 structural
and 98 in parameter descriptions, with tool descriptions, output schemas and meta
unchanged. Structural bytes move only when a tool or a parameter is added, and the
tool count never left 27, so an earlier release added parameters without saying so
here. The 5 percent margin absorbed it, which is the margin working as intended and
also the reason it went unmentioned. It was found by measuring rather than by the
test failing, and it is not attributed to a commit: the number now records what is
actually served, so the next drift is measured from the truth instead of from it.
when_the_test_fails: test_tool_payload.py fails when the live payload exceeds payload_chars * (1 +
margin), currently 23,376 chars. That headroom is about 2 average tools' worth of
text, so it absorbs a genuine feature and refuses silent drift. The surface
reached 38,843 chars precisely because nothing measured it.
1. Shrink the surface. Doctrine true of every tool belongs in SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS
in bootstrap.py, stated once, not in 27 docstrings. Error enumerations,
Returns sections and examples of the obvious can go: an agent reads an error
verbatim when it happens and does not need it described in advance.
2. Raise the number on purpose. Re-measure, update payload_chars and the
component counts here, and say in the commit message what the new bytes buy.
Do not delete the test. It is the only thing standing between this surface and
the 10,800 tokens per conversation it used to cost.
Re-measure with: uv run pytest tests/test_tool_payload.py -s
